picks.file: Aleppo ca1537 by Matrakci Nasuh Istanbul University Library ms5964.png
picks.what: Miniature in Matrakçı Nasuh’s account of Süleyman’s Iraq campaign (Istanbul University Library)
picks.why: famous color view of the walled city around the citadel mound; full two-page spread, larger than #2

picks.what: Panorama of the city with the citadel, etching after Cornelis de Bruyn in his Reizen (Rijksmuseum)
picks.who: Jan Luyken and Pieter Schenk after Cornelis de Bruyn
picks.why: wide skyline with the citadel and minarets; the companion plate #4 lacks the citadel

picks.file: Drummond, Alexander Drummond – Travels through different cities of Germany, Italy, Greece, and several parts of Asia, as far as the banks of the Euphrates, 1754 – BEIC 6247245 Aleppo.jpg
picks.what: The citadel above the city, colored engraving in Alexander Drummond’s Travels
picks.who: Johann Sebastian Müller after Alexander Drummond
picks.why: hand-colored, larger copy of #7; citadel, domes and minarets; dedication text cut

picks.file: Aleppo, Viewed from the Antioch Gate- MET DP-13897-041.jpg
picks.what: View from the Antioch Gate toward the citadel, daguerreotype (Metropolitan Museum of Art)
picks.why: earliest photograph of the city; citadel and minarets recognizable; 90 years after #6

picks.file: Aleppo and castle from southwest LCCN98506115.jpg
picks.what: The city and the citadel from the southwest, photograph (Library of Congress)
picks.why: general view with the citadel, domes and minarets; mount and caption cut

picks.what: The citadel gate, photograph (ETH Library, Zurich)
picks.why: the city’s best-known landmark, gate tower and entrance block; no general view from this period

picks.what: View over the old city from the citadel, photograph
picks.why: color view over the old city with a minaret and green dome, before the war damage

gaps: P0: no candidates; P4 has one view only
notes: P3 has two views (1754 and 1844); #5 is murky as an image, so drop it if the reviewer prefers. Skipped #9 (Matson stereo negative, catalog date ‘1900’ unreliable), #10/#14 (people at a plane landing outside the city), #12/#13 (citadel details; #11 is clearer), #15 (outer quarters), #17 (posters of the Assad family), #21 (street view), #16/#18 (2010 panoramas from the citadel are 8:1 to 9:1 strips, too narrow for a 16:9 card). Modern pick is from 1996; nothing post-war among the candidates.
